exclusion_rule: Exclude any paper that does not explicitly connect two or more depot-to-depot delivery trips to the same physical vehicle within one workday, planning horizon, or period.

records.paper: Schneider, M.; Stenger, A.; Goeke, D. (2014), The Electric Vehicle-Routing Problem with Time Windows and Recharging Stations, Transportation Science 48(4):500-520
records.evidence_checked: p.5 defines every route as starting at depot 0 and ending at depot N+1 and uses a route-level arc model without a physical-vehicle-plus-trip index or a depot-return/redeparture linkage. Its hierarchical objective minimizes the number of routes/vehicles and then distance.
records.exclusion_reason: SINGLE_TRIP_ROUTE_EQUALS_VEHICLE. Recharging-station revisits occur inside one route; the paper does not assign multiple completed depot-to-depot delivery trips to the same physical vehicle.

records.paper: Hiermann, G.; Puchinger, J.; Ropke, S.; Hartl, R. F. (2016), The Electric Fleet Size and Mix Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows and Recharging Stations, European Journal of Operational Research 252:995-1018
records.evidence_checked: p.997 asks for admissible tours so every customer is covered by exactly one tour. pp.997-998 charge vehicle acquisition cost when a route leaves the depot and formulate route columns lambda_kr; there is no physical vehicle index combined with a trip index or sequencing between depot-return tours.
records.exclusion_reason: SINGLE_TRIP_FLEET_SIZE_AND_MIX. Each selected route represents one acquired vehicle; repeated charging-station visits do not establish multiple depot-to-depot trips by one physical vehicle.

records.paper: Froger, A.; Jabali, O.; Mendoza, J. E.; Laporte, G. (2022), The Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Capacitated Charging Stations, Transportation Science 56(2):460-482
records.evidence_checked: Author-manuscript p.6 defines feasibility route by route: each route starts at the depot after time 0 and ends at the depot before T_max; the model synchronizes charging operations across routes but does not assign two completed routes to one physical EV.
records.exclusion_reason: SINGLE_TRIP_WITH_CHARGER_CONGESTION. Cross-route charger synchronization is not physical-vehicle multi-trip reuse.

records.paper: Wang, Y.; Zhou, J.; Sun, Y.; Fan, J.; Wang, Z.; Wang, H. (2023), Collaborative multidepot electric vehicle routing problem with time windows and shared charging stations, Expert Systems with Applications 219:119654
records.evidence_checked: p.5 defines x_ijv by EV v but no trip index. p.7 constrains one departure/return for EV v, and p.10 says each route starts at a depot, visits customers, and ends at a depot. There is no return-reload-redeparture sequence for the same v.
records.exclusion_reason: SINGLE_TRIP_MULTIDEPOT_EVRP. Shared charging stations and multiple depots do not make the model multi-trip.

records.paper: 陈婉茹、徐光明、张得志、曹健 (2023), 碳交易机制下多中心混合车队配送路径和速度优化研究, 系统工程理论与实践 43(11):3320-3335
records.evidence_checked: p.3322 defines the maximum load and maximum duration of one dispatch and assumes that a vehicle's trip starts and ends at the same depot. p.3324 explains constraints for a single departure, return, and one-dispatch duration; there is no physical-vehicle trip index or between-trip sequencing.
records.exclusion_reason: SINGLE_DISPATCH_MULTIDEPOT_MIXED_FLEET. It is close in depot and fleet context but does not model one physical vehicle performing multiple delivery trips in the day.
